newsitem.title: USA: Japan Airlines watches jet fuel price.
newsitem.headline: Japan Airlines watches jet fuel price.

text.p: Japan Airlines is "watching to see if the cost of fuel falls to what it was in July 1996," , Yoshi Atsumi, its cargo sales manager at Kennedy, said last Friday.
JAL charges a 10 cents per kilo fuel surcharge on cargo out of the U.S. but Atsumi said the carrier is not considering removing the surcharge on routes across the Pacific.
The carrier is forecasting a conservative increase in its import business to the U.S. of two to three percent in 1997 against 1996, Atsumi said.

JAL saw an increase in its import business of 300 tonnes, importing 1500 tonnes in March 1997 against 1200 tonnes in same 1996. Among the most imported and exported commodities were electronics, computers and machinery.
JAL exported a total of some 2200 tonnes of cargo at its John F. Kennedy facility in March of 1997 or about the same as in March 1996.

The airline is currently operating six freighter flights a week to Tokyo out of Kennedy Airport, all flown on Boeing 747 freighters. Atsumi said three of the flights are via Chicago and three via Atlanta, all six terminating at Tokyo.

The carrier, also operates 8 passenger flights on Boeing 747-400 aircraft, which have an average cargo load of about six to seven tonnes each, said Atsumi. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel +44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017
